This was not a Quiet I had known before. It was a placid current, a presence more than an absence. Everything I saw or touched or heard pulsed with a marvelous sense of order. I had a nothing mind, a flotsam mind. I was incredibly focused on the present, with very little awareness or interest in my past or future. My entire environment felt interconnected, like cells in a large, breathing organism. To experience this Quiet was to be it.
However, this sense of serenity was not shared by those around me. After I had collapsed in an Edinburgh bar while singing karaoke, and the medics had taken me away in an ambulance, my friends called my parents in the United States. It was the middle of the night in Edinburgh, but early evening in Los Angeles, and no one was overly worried about my fall from the stage, since it appeared I was suffering a simple concussion. That all changed two hours after my hospital admission—when the results of my CT scan showed the actual crisis unfolding. An aneurysm had ruptured in my brain and the hemorrhage was spreading. A neuroradiologist explained to my parents how precarious my situation was—how often people died the instant an aneurysm ruptured, and even after treatment, only slightly more than half of these patients actually survive the next few days. With every second being critical, the doctor was preparing for an emergency operation. But my now-horrified parents were stranded in California. Their passports were in their safety deposit box, and the bank branch was closed for the night. My parents rattled on the windows of the bank the next morning, successfully convincing the bank to open early for them because there was no time to waste. My procedure was well under way when my parents boarded their flight the next morning, leaving my brother and grandmother behind at the house. The operation was already over when they got to Edinburgh. My parents and friends came together, relieved that I had survived the operation, but living with a keen awareness of how perilous my situation still was.

It took a few days for me to wake up fully, under the influence of a combination of swollen brain tissue and heavy sedation. However, when I was more alert, the Quiet I found myself experiencing was much more interesting than my medical state. I had woken up to a new world, hushed and full of curiosities.
This was the very moment I became aware I couldn’t read anymore.
One of these moments of marvel took place during a move between the critical unit and the recovery ward. I was being transported in a mirrored elevator, and although there were no bandages on my face and my vision was clear, it was almost impossible for me to recognize my own reflection. Yet, somehow, this didn’t disturb me. In fact, it made remarkable sense because I was quickly realizing that my reflection was not the only thing that was different. Transformation felt abundant. Once-fixed concepts, like “wall” and “window,” weren’t as easy to identify anymore, and the differences between “he” and “she” and “I” and “it” were becoming indistinguishable. I knew my parents were my parents and my friends were my friends, but I felt less like myself and more like everything around me.
I was wheeled to a bed by a westerly-facing window, with three other women in the room. My suitemates were often in discussion with one another. Even through their brogues, I understood what they were saying, but I rarely took part in the conversations. I just enjoyed the way their voices plodded and pattered like footsteps.

The smallest of activities would enthrall me. Dressing myself, I was awed by the orbital distance between cloth and flesh. data.title: Show HN: val – An arbitrary precision calculator language
data.author: crap
data.article_summary: `val`是一个任意精度的计算器语言，基于`chumsky`和`ariadne`构建。它可以在Linux、MacOS和BSD系统上运行，最简单的安装方式是通过Rust的包管理器`cargo`。`val`提供命令行界面，支持交互式REPL环境，具有语法高亮、命令历史记录和Emacs风格编辑等功能。它不仅支持表达式计算，还支持语句构造，如`if`、`while`、`fn`等。用户可以通过命令行执行文件或直接计算表达式。此外，`val`支持多种运算符和数据类型，包括数字、布尔值、字符串和列表等，并允许函数调用和列表操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个项目中的数值计算功能及其更新和反馈

不同观点：
• primitivesuave 对 UI 表示赞赏，但指出尽管声称支持任意精度，项目仍然使用了IEEE 754双精度浮点数。他提到了一些测试如`0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3`和`2^53 == 2^53 + 1`结果为"false"，并建议如果任意精度不是关键，可以使用128位十进制浮点数来达到高精度。

• crap 感谢了反馈，并宣布项目0.3.0版本已经通过集成`astro_float`库的`BigFloat`类型实现了任意精度。他还提到目前仍在解决一些小问题，但鼓励大家尝试新功能。

• jasonjmcghee 表达了对项目相似性的兴趣，提到自己曾构建过一个类似项目，但更侧重于实时JIT评估和错误渲染，而非计算器功能。他使用了cranelift JIT，并提到了自己对错误处理的选择（miette）。

• lttlrck 对项目表示赞赏，并询问是否可以加入进制转换功能，即使是仅打印的功能也感兴趣。

• occamatl 提出了一个具体的计算问题`sqrt(10^100)-1`，结果不符合预期，暗示项目在处理大数计算时可能存在问题。

• I_complete_me 简单地对项目表示支持，提到已经在GitHub上点赞，并鼓励开发者继续努力。

补充讨论：
• 讨论的焦点之一是项目是否真正实现了任意精度计算，以及在数值计算中的实际表现是否符合用户预期。

Installation

The primary way to use

43721379.article_summary: `val`是一个任意精度的计算器语言，基于`chumsky`和`ariadne`构建。它可以在Linux、MacOS和BSD系统上运行，最简单的安装方式是通过Rust的包管理器`cargo`。`val`提供命令行界面，支持交互式REPL环境，具有语法高亮、命令历史记录和Emacs风格编辑等功能。它不仅支持表达式计算，还支持语句构造，如`if`、`while`、`fn`等。用户可以通过命令行执行文件或直接计算表达式。此外，`val`支持多种运算符和数据类型，包括数字、布尔值、字符串和列表等，并允许函数调用和列表操作。

data.title: N-Params vs. Single Param
data.author: carlos-menezes
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在TypeScript中使用多个单独参数（n params）与单个对象参数的比较。作者认为，使用对象参数通常是更好的选择，因为单独参数会导致代码可读性差，难以理解每个参数的含义，尤其在参数较多时。而使用对象参数可以使代码更清晰、自文档化，并提供更好的类型安全和自动补全功能。例如，将`createUser("John", "Doe", 28, true)`改为`createUser({ firstName: "John", lastName: "Doe", age: 28, isActive: true })`，能明确每个参数的意义，避免猜测和顺序错误。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用单一对象参数 vs 多个参数的函数定义方式，及其在不同语言和场景下的优缺点

不同观点：
• [支持单一对象参数] @disillusionist 认为使用单一对象参数让变量命名更一致，且在使用对象定义快捷方式时更自然。这种方法还能在不同方法和辅助函数中保持一致性。
• [语言差异与性能问题] @hwpythonner 指出在JS中这种模式可能更具可读性，但在C/C++等原生语言中，这种模式可能导致性能问题，如寄存器使用和结构体对齐/填充问题。不过在多层传递或需要更稳定的函数签名时，使用结构体可能更干净。
• [泛型接口的优势] @simianwords 提到这种模式可以创建泛型接口，而使用N个参数的模式无法做到这一点，因为不同实现的参数类型可能不同。
• [TypeScript的优势与现实编码] @9d 认为在TypeScript中，参数类型不同的情况下，使用对象参数可能导致不必要的复杂性，且TypeScript的自动补全和类型安全功能已经解决了大部分问题。现实编码中，这种"规则"可能并不实用。
• [长参数列表的避免] @tantalor 引用了Google的博客，强调避免长参数列表。
• [工具选择] @mx-bojangles 认为单一对象参数在某些情况下更易读，但在某些情况下，如setEnabled的例子，使用多个参数可能更直观。应根据具体情况选择最佳工具。
• [语言特性] @krystofee 指出TypeScript缺乏像Python那样的关键字参数，这也是为什么在TS中需要使用单一对象参数的原因。
• [生产代码中的唯一选择] @joeyagreco 认为在生产代码中，使用单一对象参数是处理多参数函数的唯一方式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于单一对象参数的可读性、泛型接口的创建、以及在不同语言中的性能和实用性问题。
• 一些评论者提到现实编码中TypeScript等现代工具已经能很好地解决参数类型和顺序问题，单一对象参数并非唯一选择。
• 不同语言的特性（如JS vs C++, Python的关键字参数）也影响了这种模式的适用性。
• 实际编码中，根据具体场景选择合适的方法（如单一对象参数、多个参数、或构建器模式）是多数人认同的观点。

data.title: Our quantum assembly parser got updated to the QASM 3.0 spec
data.author: msedward
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种通过TypeScript实现的与OpenQASM 3.0兼容的QASM-TS 2.0解析器，以支持量子-经典混合计算程序的验证和形式化。作者强调了这种方法对开发验证工具、编译器等的潜力，并建议使用类型论符号对OpenQASM 3.0的类型系统进行正式处理，以促进形式化验证。文章还回顾了自Quantum Hoare Logic以来的混合量子-经典计算进展。研究主题涉及编程语言和量子物理学。

Abstract:
The unique features of the hybrid quantum-classical computing model implied by the specification of OpenQASM 3.0 motivate new approaches to quantum program verification. We implement a typed QASM 3.0 parser in TypeScript to enable implementations of verification and validation software, compilers and more. We also propose that a formal treatment of OpenQASM 3.0's type system in type theory notation may further facilitate formal verification. We highlight advancements in hybrid quantum-classical computing since the Quantum Hoare Logic to this end.

data.title: There are two types of dishwasher people
data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了伴侣间因洗碗机摆放方式引发的常见争端。作者讲述了自己在2017年与男友同居后，因不擅长摆放洗碗机而引发矛盾。文章指出，许多人对如何正确摆放洗碗机感到困惑，网上充斥着大量相关建议和教程。一项针对38,000名美国成年人的调查显示，对于餐具的摆放方式没有统一意见。洗碗机的复杂性和不透明性使其成为家庭争论的焦点。文章引用专家的话解释，洗碗机的操作不易理解，且不同型号和餐具也会影响摆放方式。作者提到一个流行说法：“每段关系中，总有一人像北欧建筑师一样摆放洗碗机，而另一人则像吸毒的浣熊。”这种幽默反映出洗碗机问题在伴侣间的高度共鸣，甚至在夫妻治疗中也会被讨论。

When the couples therapist inevitably asks, I’ll have an answer ready: The trouble began in August 2017, when my boyfriend and I moved in together, and I quickly revealed myself to be an absolute ding-dong at loading the dishwasher.
I am not what you would call “precise” or “tactical” in really any aspect of my life, but certainly not in front of an open dishwasher. I lack the structural engineer’s mind for space optimization, or maybe I lack the functional adult’s patience to figure it out. I don’t totally understand how the water moves around in there, or how the soap gets dispersed. (Also, because we’re being open and honest with one another, I have never been sure about prerinsing, though I do get the sense that the rules have changed recently?) I don’t have a philosophy about what should go on the top or the bottom—I basically just put things in the first semi-logical place I see, close the door, smash some buttons, and hope for the best. I walk away and hear my plates rattle.
Judging by the sheer volume of dishwasher-loading advice, commentary, and anxiety on the internet, I am not alone in any of this. There are YouTube videos with titles such as “
You’re Doing It Wrong!
” and “
Passive Aggressive Tutorials
.” There are articles broken out by brand and by subtopic, thousands of words devoted to the intricacies of scraping, stacking, sorting, eco-washing, half loads, knives, pots, plastic, and more. There is a post from a woman who doesn’t understand how her “genius” husband “can do ANYTHING, but load a dishwasher sensibly,” and one from a person whose wife does it like “an escaped mental patient.” There are
Wirecutter
articles explaining how to use one’s dishwasher better, and people who write into
Wirecutter
to complain that they don’t like the way the dishwashers in those articles’ photos have been loaded. There are so, so many guides for couples who can’t stop fighting about the dishwasher, a large number of which suggest that the issue might not be the dishwasher at all but perhaps something with its roots in

according to
the U.S. Energy Information Administration; 19 percent of them were used zero times a week.
Dishwashers are finicky: Loading them right depends on what kind of dishes you have, what kind of mess you have, and what kind of dishwasher you have. Good Housekeeping

Men Are From Mars, Women Are From Venus

incredibly
relatable.

third

data.title: Show HN: HN Watercooler – listen to HN threads as an audio conversation
data.author: sebastiennight
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要描述了使用ElevenLabs API生成语音的过程。用户可以在输入API密钥后，指定一个Hacker News线程的URL，选择包含的评论数量，然后生成对应的对话音频。文章提到生成过程分为几个步骤：开始生成对话、处理中、以及最终生成音频文件供下载。整个过程旨在将在线讨论转换为语音格式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对文本转语音软件的功能反馈与改进建议，尤其是如何提升对话的自然性和使用体验。

不同观点：
• sebastiennight：提出几个问题和功能请求，包括不使用低质量的Legacy语音、减少重复的自我介绍、强调引用、增加音频章节标记、为特定用户名分配语音以及添加音效。他还特别关注如何让对话听起来更加自然。
• rgbrgb：对功能表示兴趣，并询问是否有示例可以参考。
• gojomo：询问是否可以上传自己的声音样本以用于评论，以及是否可以通过语音命令进行导航，特别是在驾驶时使用。
• mosquitobiten：建议将长篇回复分割成多条对话，以模拟自然的辩论形式，而不是单一的演讲形式。
• wewewedxfgdf：认为该功能可以作为播客的替代品，甚至建议将其发布为播客。
• plun9：发现生成的音频中评论数量少了一个，存在技术问题。
• devrandoom：对功能表示赞赏，但用比喻（泥泞的水）暗示对功能完善性的担忧。
• thegreatpeter：用夸张的表情（撕头发）表达对复杂问题的无奈或不满。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：目前功能在语音质量和对话自然性上存在不足。用户对如何提升体验有不同建议，例如减少重复内容、增加音效和章节标记等。
• 技术问题：plun9指出了评论数量不匹配的技术问题，这可能影响用户体验。
• 个性化需求：gojomo提出了对个性化声音和语音命令的需求，显示出用户对功能定制化的期待。
• 自然对话：多个用户（sebastiennight和mosquitobiten）强调了让对话更加自然的重要性，这可能是未来改进的重点。

data.title: AGI Is Still 30 Years Away – Ege Erdil and Tamay Besiroglu
data.author: Philpax
data.article_summary: 在这期Dwarkesh Podcast中，Ege Erdil和Tamay Besiroglu讨论了对AGI（通用人工智能）发展时间的预测以及其潜在影响。他们认为AGI仍需30年才能实现，并质疑“智能爆炸”理论，认为经济各领域的协同变化将推动经济增长，而不仅仅是智能的提升。他们将此比作工业革命，强调了多方面创新带来的综合效应。此外，他们创立了Mechanize，旨在完全自动化工作流程。对于AGI实现后的经济影响，他们预期会出现爆炸性经济增长，并探讨了中央计划在AGI时代是否可行。他们也提供了职业建议，并讨论了AI领域中的竞争动态和超级智能的真实性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AGI（通用人工智能）的实现时间、重要性、当前AI技术的实用性以及对社会的影响。

不同观点：
• yibg认为，没有人知道实现AGI需要多长时间，因为我们尚未清楚人类智能的本质，且历史表明AGI总是被认为在几十年后才能实现。
• ksec质疑AGI的重要性，认为未来10到15年将是辅助智能的时代，当前的LLM（大型语言模型）虽然有不足，但已经能提高生产力，可能导致人类生产工作的结束。
• codingwagie分享了使用当前AI工具（如o3）设计复杂系统的成功经验，暗示当前AI已经非常实用。
• dicroce认为，现在AI的能力需要十年或更长时间才能完全消化，暗示实现AGI并不紧迫。
• lucisferre以幽默的方式将AGI的实现时间与实用的核聚变反应堆相提并论，暗示两者都遥遥无期。
• dcchambers断言LLM永远不会成为AGI，并认为当前对LLM的 obsession 可能会阻碍AGI的实现，批评AI公司只关注商业利益。
• xnx引用Demis Hassabis的观点，认为AGI将在5-10年内实现，与dcchambers的观点形成对比。
• fusionadvocate对Dwarkesh人物的背景和影响力提出质疑，偏离了主要讨论点。
• csours强调AI研究需要 embodiment（实体化）来证明其理解和改变物理世界的能力。
• Zambyte提到了“AI效应”，即人们常常低估当前AI的能力。
• EliRivers提出一个问题：如果AGI真的出现了，我们能识别出来吗？

补充讨论：
• 关于AGI实现时间的争议是核心焦点，yibg和dcchambers持怀疑态度，而xnx则引用权威人物的乐观预测。
• ksec对当前AI技术的实际应用持积极态度，认为即使没有AGI，AI也已经显著提高了生产力。
• csours提出的AI研究需要 embodiment 的观点提供了一个新的视角，强调了AI与物理世界交互的重要性。
• 讨论中还涉及到对Dwarkesh人物背景的质疑，虽然这偏离了主要讨论点，但也显示出社区对人物影响力和动机的关注。

整体来看，评论中对于AGI的实现时间、当前AI技术的实用性以及AGI的重要性存在较大分歧，并且对AI研究的方向和目标也有不同见解。

AGI will take another 3 decades
Dwarkesh Patel
00:00:00
Today, I’m chatting with
Tamay Besiroglu
and
Ege Erdil
. They were previously running
Epoch AI
and are now launching Mechanize, which is a company dedicated to automating all work. One of the interesting points you made recently, Tamay, is that the whole idea of the intelligence explosion is mistaken or misleading. Why don’t you explain what you’re talking about there?
Tamay Besiroglu
00:00:22
Yeah, I think it’s not a very useful concept. It’s kind of like calling the Industrial Revolution a horsepower explosion. Sure, during the Industrial Revolution, we saw this drastic acceleration in raw physical power, but there are many other things that were maybe equally important in explaining the acceleration of growth and technological change that we saw during the Industrial Revolution.
Dwarkesh Patel
00:00:42
What is a way to characterize the broader set of things that the horsepower perspective would miss about the Industrial Revolution?
Tamay Besiroglu
00:00:50
So I think in the case of the Industrial Revolution, it was a bunch of these complementary changes to many different sectors in the economy. So you had agriculture, you had transportation, you had law and finance, you had urbanization and moving from rural areas into cities. There were just many different innovations that happened simultaneously that gave rise to this change in the way of economically organizing our society.
It wasn’t just that we had more horsepower. I mean, that was part of it, but that’s not the kind of central thing to focus on when thinking about the Industrial Revolution. And I think similarly, for the development of AI, sure, we’ll get a lot of very smart AI systems, but that will be one part among very many different moving parts that explain why we expect to get this transition and this acceleration and growth and technological change.
Dwarkesh Patel
00:01:46
I want to better understand how you think about that broader transformation. Before we do, the other really interesting part of your worldview is that you have longer timelines to get to AGI than most of the people in San Francisco who think about AI. When do you expect a drop-in remote worker replacement?
Ege Erdil
00:02:05
Maybe for me,

补充讨论：
• 关于AGI实现时间的争议是核心焦点，yibg和dcchambers持怀疑态度，而xnx则引用权威人物的乐观预测。
• ksec对当前AI技术的实际应用持积极态度，认为即使没有AGI，AI也已经显著提高了生产力。
• csours提出的AI研究需要 embodiment 的观点提供了一个新的视角，强调了AI与物理世界交互的重要性。
• 讨论中还涉及到对Dwarkesh人物背景的质疑，虽然这偏离了主要讨论点，但也显示出社区对人物影响力和动机的关注。

整体来看，评论中对于AGI的实现时间、当前AI技术的实用性以及AGI的重要性存在较大分歧，并且对AI研究的方向和目标也有不同见解。

• **[jjice]** 担心面部识别技术在判断用户年龄时的准确性，特别是对于那些外表与实际年龄不符的用户。如果识别错误，用户可能被锁定，甚至需要提供身份证件，这引发了对新规的质疑。

• **[Retr0id]** 拒绝接受面部扫描，并考虑使用技术手段绕过验证。这种反对是基于原则，不愿意让服务提供商获取其生物特征数据。

• **[rkagerer]** 强烈反对让孩子进行面部扫描，并表示在金融公司要求类似验证时也曾拒绝。其反对的核心在于对隐私和数据安全的担忧。

• **[MiddleEndian]** 直接呼吁立法禁止面部扫描，认为这是保护隐私的必要措施。

• **[hedora]** 讨论了在工作中应对这种验证要求的实际困难，建议通过技术手段（如VPN和地理封锁）规避，并希望国际技术社区共同施压，促使英国撤销此类法律。

• **[nyanpasu64]** 担心这种验证方式会剥夺未成年人的网络权利，特别是那些生活在不安全环境中的青少年。网络支持网络对这些青少年的心理健康至关重要。

• **[zevv]** 希望找到一种不涉及发送面部照片或护照的技术来验证年龄，表明用户对隐私保护的高度关注。

• **[MisterTea]** 提到像IRC这样的平台由于缺乏某些功能，反而避免了成人内容验证的问题，暗示简单技术有时能避免复杂问题。

• **[nixpulves]** 认为身份验证问题一直没有解决，任何改进尝试都带有威权性质，而现状又为规避行为留有空间。个人怀念过去匿名交流的时代。

• **[nubinetwork]** 明确表示，如果Discord要求提供照片，将关闭账户，表明对隐私的极度重视。

补充讨论：
• **[acureau]** 提到，Discord的用户中可能有很大一部分是未成年人，这些用户可能会因为新规而转向其他平台。这暗示了平台用户流失的可能性。

争议焦点：
• 年龄验证的必要性与隐私保护之间的平衡。
• 面部识别技术的准确性与潜在误用。
• 政府与第三方对用户数据的获取和使用。
• 新技术和加密手段能否提供有效的隐私保护解决方案。

43715884.article_content:
Discord's face scanning age checks 'start of a bigger shift'
3 hours ago
Share
Save
Imran Rahman-Jones & Chris Vallance
Technology reporters
Share
Save
Getty Images
Discord is testing face scanning to verify some users' ages in the UK and Australia.
The social platform, which says it has over 200 million monthly users around the world, was initially used by gamers but now has communities on a wide range of topics including pornography.
The UK's online safety laws mean platforms with adult content will need to have "robust" age verification
in place by July
.
And social media expert Matt Navarra told the BBC "this isn't a one-off - it's the start of a bigger shift".
"Regulators want real proof, and facial recognition might be the fastest route there," he said.
But campaigners have said these types of checks are ineffective and could lead to privacy issues.
"Age assurance is becoming the new seatbelt for the internet," said Mr Navarra.
"Will it become the norm in the UK? Honestly, yes, probably."
He said he believed the incoming changes in online safety laws mean online platforms would beef up their age verification processes.
"The era of 'click here to confirm you're 13' is dead," he said.
"Get age verification wrong now, and you don't just lose users - you could lose a courtroom battle or incur fines."
Firms which do not comply with the Online Safety Act could be fined up to 10% of their global turnover.
Instagram previously brought in
age checks using facial analysis
in 2022 for users who want to change their profile settings to be over 18.
The social media company requires users to take a selfie video on their phone and uses AI to estimate the person's age.
Like Discord, they can alternatively upload a picture of their photo ID.
How can you keep your child safe online?
The US-based platform says the verification - which it describes as "an experiment" - will be a one-time check.
It will apply the first time a user comes across content which it has flagged as sensitive, or if they change their settings on viewing sensitive media.
Users can either use the face scanner or upload a photo of their ID to confirm their age.
It says information used for age checks will not be stored by Discord or the verification company.
Face scans will stay on the device and not be collected, and ID uploads will be deleted after the verification is complete,
according to the company
.
Content which is flagged as sensitive is already automatically blocked or blurred for teenagers.
'No silver bullet'
Privacy campaign group Big Brother Watch says age check technology "shouldn't be seen as a silver bullet solution".
Senior advocacy officer Madeleine Stone says they can pose a risk to users, "including security breaches, privacy intrusion, errors, digital exclusion and censorship".
While industry group the Age Verification Providers Association says there is a "wide range of convenient, privacy-preserving methods".
Their executive director Iain Corby told the BBC the latest technology can estimate age "within one to two years based on a selfie or how you move your hands".
But he also said platforms have a choice on how to use age verification.
"They can remove the harmful content altogether, apply age checks to access the whole site, or just check ages before allowing access to high-risk pages and posts," he said.
Australia is planning to bring in a social media ban for all under-16s this year.
Recent research
found more than 80% of Australian children aged eight to 12 use social media or messaging services that are only meant to be for over-13s
New Jersey attorney general Matthew J. Platkin said on Thursday that his office was suing Discord, alleging the company had misled parents about its safety controls and the risks faced by children on the app.
Discord was approached for comment.

data.title: Snapchat is harming children at an industrial scale?
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 文章指出，Snap Inc.（Snapchat的母公司）在其产品设计上导致数百万儿童面临伤害。调查显示，Snapchat每月收到约1万起关于性勒索的举报，但这可能只是实际发生的一小部分。文章引用了多起法律诉讼，指控Snapchat的功能助长了针对青少年的多种伤害，包括成瘾性使用、药物与枪支问题、儿童性虐待、性勒索、网络霸凌等。内部报告和员工对话显示，公司高管了解这些问题，但未及时采取有效措施。例如，其年龄验证系统被承认无效，无法阻止未成年用户注册。文章呼吁家长关注这些信息，以更好地保护孩子。尽管Snap Inc.试图驳斥部分指控，但文章认为现有证据揭示了公司对未成年用户的深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体（特别是Snapchat）对用户健康和行为的影响，以及平台的商业模式和监管问题。

不同观点：
• [aylmao] 认为公司使用“健康”这个词来讨论用户参与度和留存率，而不是用户的个人健康。这种语言可能会引导员工更多关注产品成功而非用户福祉。
• [adityapuranik] 分享了个人经历，指出Snapchat的连续天数（streak）功能带来了社交压力，并描述了如何通过停止使用该功能来解脱。这种行为在用户中可能普遍存在。
• [peterbecich] 引用统计数据，指出青少年每天收到大量智能手机通知，并认为这些通知的长期价值有限，可能对年轻人产生负面影响。
• [zonkerdonker] 建议在社交媒体平台上引入地理围栏技术，以限制其在特定区域（如学校）的使用，从而减少不良内容对青少年的影响。
• [neilv] 质疑为什么员工会撰写管理层不愿意听到的负面报告，并提出了几种可能性，包括职业安全、信息透明度以及自我保护等。
• [WaitWaitWha] 强调社交媒体对儿童和年轻人在社交技能和现实后果认知方面的负面影响，并指出简单的解决方案不足以解决这些问题。
• [Nevermark] 认为社交媒体的商业模式本质上存在巨大的利益冲突，建议通过法律手段限制这种商业模式，并提出更健康的社交媒体形式。
• [rattlesnakedave] 指出Snapchat的“探索”功能推送不当内容且无法关闭，认为这是平台的一个显著问题。
• [burningChrome] 提问是否社交媒体的负面影响已经到了临界点，暗示可能需要更广泛的变革。
• [cbruns] 直接质问在Snap工作的读者是否对自己的工作感到安心，暗示对平台道德问题的关注。
• [Frieren] 认为当前一代父母未能识别社交媒体对孩子的危险，并呼吁加强监管以保护消费者，特别是儿童。
• [ViktorRay] 引用《黑镜》剧集，指出Snapchat等社交媒体的负面影响正在发生，而社会未能有效应对，呼应了《黑镜》中的情节。
• [heavyset_go] 提到研究发现Snapchat是儿童性虐待材料（CSAM）生产和分发的主要渠道，并指出该平台在网络诱骗中的角色。

补充讨论：
• 关于Snapchat原始设计意图和功能变化的讨论，[neilv] 提到Snapchat最初可能被设计用于成人之间的私密交流，但后来功能发生了变化。
• 多个评论提到了社交媒体平台对青少年和儿童的负面影响，包括成瘾性、社交压力和不当内容，呼吁更严格的监管和更健康的平台设计。
• 争议的焦点主要集中在社交媒体对个人和社会的负面影响，以及平台公司是否应对此负责并采取行动。

In their own words, we see that Snap Inc’s design choices expose millions of kids to harm

and

28

Introduction
Source: Shutterstock
On October 1, 2024, investigative journalist Jeff Horwitz
reported
a startling statistic from an internal Snap Inc. email quoted in a court case against Snap Inc., the company which owns Snapchat. The email noted that the company receives around 10,000 reports of sextortion
each month
—and that figure is likely “only a fraction of the total abuse occurring on the platform.”
This statistic prompted us to investigate what else Snap Inc. knows or believes about the impact of its product on users, particularly teens (We
estimate
that roughly 13 million American 13-17 year-olds use Snapchat). Over the past several months, we have examined multiple court cases filed against Snap Inc., many involving severe or fatal harm that was (allegedly) facilitated by Snapchat’s features. From 2022 through 2025, as part of the Multidistrict Litigation (MDL) and Judicial Council Coordinated Proceedings (JCCP) against social media defendants, more than 600
1
such lawsuits specifically named Snap Inc. as a defendant. In addition, state attorneys general from
Nevada
and
New Mexico
have brought significant cases against the company—two cases which we will draw heavily from in this post.
Following the format of our previous post about the
“industrial scale harms” attributed to TikTok
, this piece presents dozens of quotations from internal reports, studies, memos, conversations, and public statements in which Snap executives, employees, and consultants acknowledge and discuss the harms that Snapchat causes to many minors who use their platform. We group these findings into five key clusters of harms:
Addictive, Compulsive, and Problematic Use
Drugs and Guns
Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM), Sextortion, and In-person Sexual Predation and Assault
Cyberbullying
Knowledge of Harm and Underage Use, and Lack of Action
Similar to TikTok, we show that company insiders were aware of multiple widespread and serious harms, and in many cases did not act promptly or make substantial changes. As Snap’s director of security engineering said regarding Android users who are selling drugs or child sexual abuse material on Snap:
“That’s fine it’s been broken for ten years we can tolerate tonight.”
2
With regard to sextortion on the platform, one employee had complained in a private channel:
“God I’m so pissed that were over-run by this sextortion shit right now. We’ve twiddled our thumbs and wrung our hands all f…ing year.”
3
The briefs allege that the company is also aware of rampant underage use, and of the ineffectiveness of their age gating process. Snap executives have admitted that Snapchat’s age verification system
“Is effectively useless in stopping underage users from signing up to the Snapchat app.”
4
Although the evidence below is all publicly available, no one has compiled and combined direct quotations from company insiders and internal reports across multiple alleged harms. We think this compilation gives vital information to parents, who might want some insight into the business practices of a company that hosts their children’s social lives, owns much of their attention, and influences their social development.
At the start of each section, we highlight a real-life example—drawn from relevant court documents—illustrating the specific harm in question. Each child’s story offers a human perspective on the broader statistics and quotations that reveal the far-reaching harms discussed within the company.
Subscribe
1. Our Conversations with Snap, Inc.
While working on this post we had four conversations with Snap’s leaders and employees during which we asked them about some of the harms that appear in the various briefs. In three of those meetings, we asked specifically about the claim, taken from an internal Snap email that was quoted in the New Mexico brief, that Snap gets 10,000 reports of sextortion each month. We did not get any rebuttals or explanations of that claim.
Snap’s Trust and Safety team made a point that we think is valid and important for readers to keep in mind: the briefs we are drawing from present the allegations of one side in litigation, and there is often another side. Some of the quotations may have been misinterpreted or taken out of context. Snap’s Trust and Safety team pointed us to a
motion
Snap made to have the New Mexico case dismissed. We read that brief and found that it contested only a few of the many claims made in the New Mexico brief. Two of these claims had been in our list of quotations, so we cut one from the post below, and we added a comment
43704382.article_summary: 文章指出，Snap Inc.（Snapchat的母公司）在其产品设计上导致数百万儿童面临伤害。调查显示，Snapchat每月收到约1万起关于性勒索的举报，但这可能只是实际发生的一小部分。文章引用了多起法律诉讼，指控Snapchat的功能助长了针对青少年的多种伤害，包括成瘾性使用、药物与枪支问题、儿童性虐待、性勒索、网络霸凌等。内部报告和员工对话显示，公司高管了解这些问题，但未及时采取有效措施。例如，其年龄验证系统被承认无效，无法阻止未成年用户注册。文章呼吁家长关注这些信息，以更好地保护孩子。尽管Snap Inc.试图驳斥部分指控，但文章认为现有证据揭示了公司对未成年用户的深远影响。
43704382.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体（特别是Snapchat）对用户健康和行为的影响，以及平台的商业模式和监管问题。

不同观点：
• [aylmao] 认为公司使用“健康”这个词来讨论用户参与度和留存率，而不是用户的个人健康。这种语言可能会引导员工更多关注产品成功而非用户福祉。
• [adityapuranik] 分享了个人经历，指出Snapchat的连续天数（streak）功能带来了社交压力，并描述了如何通过停止使用该功能来解脱。这种行为在用户中可能普遍存在。
• [peterbecich] 引用统计数据，指出青少年每天收到大量智能手机通知，并认为这些通知的长期价值有限，可能对年轻人产生负面影响。
• [zonkerdonker] 建议在社交媒体平台上引入地理围栏技术，以限制其在特定区域（如学校）的使用，从而减少不良内容对青少年的影响。
• [neilv] 质疑为什么员工会撰写管理层不愿意听到的负面报告，并提出了几种可能性，包括职业安全、信息透明度以及自我保护等。
• [WaitWaitWha] 强调社交媒体对儿童和年轻人在社交技能和现实后果认知方面的负面影响，并指出简单的解决方案不足以解决这些问题。
• [Nevermark] 认为社交媒体的商业模式本质上存在巨大的利益冲突，建议通过法律手段限制这种商业模式，并提出更健康的社交媒体形式。
• [rattlesnakedave] 指出Snapchat的“探索”功能推送不当内容且无法关闭，认为这是平台的一个显著问题。
• [burningChrome] 提问是否社交媒体的负面影响已经到了临界点，暗示可能需要更广泛的变革。
• [cbruns] 直接质问在Snap工作的读者是否对自己的工作感到安心，暗示对平台道德问题的关注。
• [Frieren] 认为当前一代父母未能识别社交媒体对孩子的危险，并呼吁加强监管以保护消费者，特别是儿童。
• [ViktorRay] 引用《黑镜》剧集，指出Snapchat等社交媒体的负面影响正在发生，而社会未能有效应对，呼应了《黑镜》中的情节。
• [heavyset_go] 提到研究发现Snapchat是儿童性虐待材料（CSAM）生产和分发的主要渠道，并指出该平台在网络诱骗中的角色。

补充讨论：
• 关于Snapchat原始设计意图和功能变化的讨论，[neilv] 提到Snapchat最初可能被设计用于成人之间的私密交流，但后来功能发生了变化。
• 多个评论提到了社交媒体平台对青少年和儿童的负面影响，包括成瘾性、社交压力和不当内容，呼吁更严格的监管和更健康的平台设计。
• 争议的焦点主要集中在社交媒体对个人和社会的负面影响，以及平台公司是否应对此负责并采取行动。

data.author: jsomers
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一项基础科学发现的描述及其跨学科比较

不同观点：
• [观点一：积极评价] biomcgary认为这篇文章很好地描述了一个近期的基础科学发现。尽管文章中包含一些专业术语，可能让非生物学背景的人难以理解，但整体上传达了生物学发现和验证过程的复杂性和逻辑性。
  
• [观点二：跨学科比较] 作为计算生物学家，biomcgary还提到生物学中的假设生成与验证逻辑，与计算机科学（CS）中的算法开发有相似之处。他认为在两个领域中，提出重要的大问题都是至关重要的。

补充讨论：
• [发现的重要性] biomcgary指出，有些科学发现虽然起初看似 obscure（不起眼），但其重要性和应用可能会在后来被认识到。例如，CRISPR 技术和青霉素的发现与应用，或 Google 对 Transformer 模型的开发与其在 OpenAI 的应用之间的对比。

• [争议焦点] 虽然评论中未直接出现争议，但可以推断出潜在的讨论点在于文章的专业术语使用上。biomcgary 提到非生物学背景的读者可能不易理解，暗示了对科学传播清晰度的关注。

总结：这则评论既表达了对科学发现的赞赏，又通过跨学科视角讨论了科学发现和算法开发的相似性，并通过具体例子强调了某些发现的长远影响。

data.title: Show HN: Zuni (YC S24) – AI Copilot for the Browser
data.author: willgtaylor
data.article_summary: Zuni 是一款 Chrome 浏览器侧边栏的 AI 工具，支持最新的人工智能模型，如 OpenAI、Anthropic 等，并能从用户打开的标签页和 Gmail 中获取上下文，帮助回答问题和撰写邮件。它提供免费和付费版本，付费版每月20美元，包含更多消息额度和优先访问新模型的权限。用户可以获得更高效的电子邮件助理功能，如摘要、建议和草稿回复。Zuni 还提供首月无条件退款保证，并且按月订阅，无年度承诺。如果超出消息额度，需升级计划或等待额度重置。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新推出的AI产品的功能、市场定位、技术实现及定价策略

不同观点：
• [产品市场前景的担忧 - joshdavham]  
  - 观点：担心Google的新产品Gemini和其将AI整合进Google Workspace的策略可能会吞噬该产品的市场。  
  - 论据：Gemini和Google Workspace的整合可能带来竞争压力，并提出可以考虑在其他浏览器或服务（如Proton Mail on Firefox）中寻找市场切入点。

• [产品功能不足的批评 - WillPostForFood]  
  - 观点：认为产品无法访问浏览器内容，导致其实用性有限。  
  - 例子：通过与Zuni的对话，发现该产品无法查看用户的浏览器内容，从而认为其“毫无意义”。

• [对产品定位和期望的失望 - bluelightning2k]  
  - 观点：认为产品宣传与实际功能不符，期望的“自动化”功能未能实现。  
  - 论据：实际功能仅为Gmail的辅助工具，而非全面自动化工具，且需要安装浏览器扩展，不如官方工具直接。

• [对产品展示和用例的反馈 - serjester]  
  - 观点：产品着陆页未能有效展示核心卖点，视频内容更像是实施细节而非吸引用户的亮点。  
  - 论据：视频内容展示的用例（如通过Stripe网站建立C Corp）并不实用，用户更可能直接向LLM提问。

• [对定价和透明度的不满 - joshstrange]  
  - 观点：认为产品定价过高且不透明，特别是“Message Credits”的定义不明确。  
  - 论据：每月20美元的费用对于一个仅比复制粘贴多一步的工具来说过高，且没有明确的限制说明。

补充讨论：
• [积极的反馈和支持 - ksvarma]  
  - 观点：对产品表示看好，愿意尝试。  
  - 例子：简单表示产品看起来不错，并祝好运。

• [技术实现的兴趣 - joshdavham]  
  - 观点：对浏览器扩展的实现细节感兴趣，特别是如何处理认证、MV3合规、处理不同标签页等问题。  
  - 论据：基于自身开发复杂Chrome扩展的经验，认为一般开发者可能不了解浏览器扩展开发的“非标准”性质。

争议焦点：
• 产品的市场定位和Google等大公司产品可能带来的竞争压力。  
• 产品功能是否如宣传所言，特别是无法访问浏览器内容导致的实用性问题。  
• 定价策略和功能价值是否匹配，特别是“Message Credits”的定义和收费合理性。

data.title: mIRC 7.81
data.author: futurecat
data.article_summary: mIRC是一款广泛使用的互联网中继聊天（IRC）客户端，已有二十多年历史，适用于个人和组织在全球IRC网络上进行交流、分享、娱乐和工作。它功能强大、可靠且有趣。最新版本mIRC v7.81已发布，用户可以加入发布通知邮件列表以获取更新信息。此外，用户可以在讨论论坛中交流或寻求帮助。版权归mIRC公司所有（1995-2025）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对mIRC（及相关技术）的怀旧情感、当前使用情况、以及对其授权模式变化的看法。

不同观点：
• [怀旧与正面评价]  
   多位用户（如[diggan], [alecsm], [marsavar], [bn-l], [ceautery]）分享了他们对mIRC的美好回忆，特别是在90年代和2000年代的经历。mIRC的脚本功能、定制性以及IRC聊天室带来的社区感被多次提到。  
   例子：[alecsm]提到自己通过mIRC脚本编写简单的AI机器人，[ceautery]分享了开发"JoTrivia"脚本的经历。

• [对mIRC授权模式变化的不满]  
   [Urgo]指出mIRC在2016年将原本的“终身授权”改为“每年授权”的做法让人不满，认为这破坏了早期用户的信任。他建议mIRC应该尊重之前的终身授权协议。  
   例子：[Urgo]引用了mIRC官网在2016年前后的变化，以证明其授权模式的转变。

• [对现代IRC客户端及平台的讨论]  
   一些用户（如[diggan], [aaronmdjones]）提到现代的IRC客户端如HexChat和WeeChat，并讨论了这些开源、跨平台的替代品。部分用户认为这些新平台可以作为mIRC的继承者。  
   例子：[diggan]推荐HexChat，并询问是否有其他活跃的分支，[aaronmdjones]则表示自己使用WeeChat并持续使用IRC。

• [对mIRC现状的感慨与反思]  
   部分用户（如[nobleach], [keyle]）表达了对mIRC及其时代的怀旧情绪，认为mIRC如果在今天可能会更受欢迎或更有价值。  
   例子：[nobleach]提到会去bash.org怀旧，[keyle]认为mIRC如果在今天会值很多钱。

补充讨论：
• [技术细节与趣闻]  
   用户分享了关于mIRC技术细节的趣闻，例如[Thoreandan]提到在“关于”页面点击开发者鼻子会发出吱吱声的彩蛋，[patwolf]则回忆了每个版本更新时开发者照片的变化。  

• [对IRC社群变化的看法]  
   有用户（如[crazymoka], [languagehacker]）提到IRC服务器和社区的变化，例如Freenode服务器和DALnet被DDoS攻击，导致他们减少或停止了mIRC的使用。

争议焦点：
• mIRC授权模式的改变（从终身授权到年度授权）引发了部分老用户的不满，认为这种做法不尊重早期用户的信任和投资。

43715306.article_summary: mIRC是一款广泛使用的互联网中继聊天（IRC）客户端，已有二十多年历史，适用于个人和组织在全球IRC网络上进行交流、分享、娱乐和工作。它功能强大、可靠且有趣。最新版本mIRC v7.81已发布，用户可以加入发布通知邮件列表以获取更新信息。此外，用户可以在讨论论坛中交流或寻求帮助。版权归mIRC公司所有（1995-2025）。
43715306.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对mIRC（及相关技术）的怀旧情感、当前使用情况、以及对其授权模式变化的看法。

不同观点：
• [怀旧与正面评价]  
   多位用户（如[diggan], [alecsm], [marsavar], [bn-l], [ceautery]）分享了他们对mIRC的美好回忆，特别是在90年代和2000年代的经历。mIRC的脚本功能、定制性以及IRC聊天室带来的社区感被多次提到。  
   例子：[alecsm]提到自己通过mIRC脚本编写简单的AI机器人，[ceautery]分享了开发"JoTrivia"脚本的经历。

• [对mIRC授权模式变化的不满]  
   [Urgo]指出mIRC在2016年将原本的“终身授权”改为“每年授权”的做法让人不满，认为这破坏了早期用户的信任。他建议mIRC应该尊重之前的终身授权协议。  
   例子：[Urgo]引用了mIRC官网在2016年前后的变化，以证明其授权模式的转变。

• [对现代IRC客户端及平台的讨论]  
   一些用户（如[diggan], [aaronmdjones]）提到现代的IRC客户端如HexChat和WeeChat，并讨论了这些开源、跨平台的替代品。部分用户认为这些新平台可以作为mIRC的继承者。  
   例子：[diggan]推荐HexChat，并询问是否有其他活跃的分支，[aaronmdjones]则表示自己使用WeeChat并持续使用IRC。

• [对mIRC现状的感慨与反思]  
   部分用户（如[nobleach], [keyle]）表达了对mIRC及其时代的怀旧情绪，认为mIRC如果在今天可能会更受欢迎或更有价值。  
   例子：[nobleach]提到会去bash.org怀旧，[keyle]认为mIRC如果在今天会值很多钱。

补充讨论：
• [技术细节与趣闻]  
   用户分享了关于mIRC技术细节的趣闻，例如[Thoreandan]提到在“关于”页面点击开发者鼻子会发出吱吱声的彩蛋，[patwolf]则回忆了每个版本更新时开发者照片的变化。  

• [对IRC社群变化的看法]  
   有用户（如[crazymoka], [languagehacker]）提到IRC服务器和社区的变化，例如Freenode服务器和DALnet被DDoS攻击，导致他们减少或停止了mIRC的使用。

争议焦点：
• mIRC授权模式的改变（从终身授权到年度授权）引发了部分老用户的不满，认为这种做法不尊重早期用户的信任和投资。

data.author: Bluestein

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI是否处于经济泡沫中及其对社会的影响

不同观点：
• [mrandish] 认为大多数技术专家都认为AI目前处于显著的金融泡沫中，质疑是否有不同的看法。
• [jaredcwhite] 强烈批评大科技公司，认为AI和自动化内容正在破坏开放网络，并期待这些公司为其“数字罪行”负责的那一天。
• [metalman] 指出大量AI生成的内容没有价值，缺乏人工审查和编辑，且这种趋势可能会持续，因为生产成本会越来越低。不过，他也提到这种现象可能让某些精神疾病患者显得更正常，这是一种奇怪的社会平衡。
• [camillomiller] 表示对AI带来的“清算”时刻充满期待，支持对当前AI趋势进行反思或纠正。
• [quantified] 引用Ed Zitron的观点，认为AI相关的内容是针对不阅读、不倾听或不了解信息的人群制作的，并将其比作美国政治信息，暗示其具有宣传性质。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI生成内容的质量及其社会影响。一部分人认为这是无价值的内容泛滥，另一部分人则关注其对社会行为的潜在影响。
• 讨论中还涉及对大科技公司的不满和对AI经济泡沫的预期，反映出对当前技术发展方向的深切担忧。
• 不同评论者对AI未来的态度各异，从期待泡沫破裂到认为AI带来的怪异社会现象会持续存在，观点多样。

data.title: OpenAI Codex CLI: Lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: OpenAI Codex CLI是一款轻量级编码工具，可在终端运行，支持开发者通过ChatGPT级别的推理能力执行代码、操作文件和版本控制。它处于实验开发阶段，可能包含漏洞或不完整功能。安装方式为通过`npm install -g @openai/codex`全局安装，并设置OpenAI API密钥。Codex支持交互式和非交互式运行，可自动生成代码、安装依赖并展示结果，同时通过沙盒机制确保安全。用户可选择不同的审批模式控制其自主性，如"Suggest"、"Auto Edit"和"Full Auto"模式，其中"Full Auto"模式下所有操作都在禁用网络和目录沙盒中进行，确保安全。Codex还提供多模态支持，允许输入截图或图表来实现功能，并完全开源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同代码生成工具（如Codex、Claude Code等）的性能、使用体验和优缺点比较。

不同观点：
• **Codex与Claude Code的性能对比**：
  - [gklitt] 认为Claude Code在文档生成方面表现优于Codex，Codex出现了虚构代码和错误描述架构的问题。
  - [cube2222] 对Claude Code的表现感到惊喜，认为其生成的PR质量高，尽管成本较高但效率显著。
  - [mgdev] 认为Codex目前表现不如Claude Code，但希望开源后能迅速改进。

• **开源与专有工具的争议**：
  - [999900000999] 偏好开源工具，认为专有工具如Claude Code限制了模型选择自由，且Deepseek等开源工具更具性价比。
  - [gizmodo59] 赞赏Codex的开源性质，认为这是相较于Claude Code的一大优势。

• **工具使用体验与技术问题**：
  - [kumarm] 在使用Codex时遇到了模型选择和崩溃等问题，但初步使用后认为其表现尚可。
  - [asadm] 使用自定义脚本将整个代码库粘贴到Gemini中并应用更改，认为其他工具如Aider/Copilot等各有不足。

• **工具的灵活性与模型选择**：
  - [baalimago] 自制的Clai工具允许自由更换模型，认为这是相较于其他工具的一大优势。
  - [flakiness] 提供了Codex CLI的详细提示模板，展示了工具如何在实际操作中执行任务。

补充讨论：
• **隐私与安全问题**：
  - [est] 指出Codex工具会上传代码到在线API，提醒用户注意代码隐私。

• **工具的经济性与成本**：
  - [cube2222] 认为Claude Code的高成本在效率提升面前是可接受的，期望未来能解决成本问题。
  - [999900000999] 提到Deepseek的成本远低于Claude Code，且性能差距不大。

争议焦点：
• **Codex与Claude Code的性能与成本对比**：不同用户对这两个工具的性能和成本有不同看法，部分用户认为Claude Code表现更好但成本高，而Codex的开源性质和未来改进潜力被一些用户看好。

• **开源与专有工具的选择**：部分用户偏好开源工具，认为其更具灵活性和性价比，而专有工具的限制（如模型选择）成为争议点。

Experimental Technology Disclaimer
Codex CLI is an experimental project under active development. It is not yet stable, may contain bugs, incomplete features, or undergo breaking changes. We’re building it in the open with the community and welcome:
Bug reports
Feature requests
Pull requests
Good vibes
Help us improve by filing issues or submitting PRs (see the section below for how to contribute)!
Quickstart
Install globally:
npm install -g @openai/codex
Next, set your OpenAI API key as an environment variable:
export
OPENAI_API_KEY=
"
your-api-key-here
"
Note:
This command sets the key only for your current terminal session. To make it permanent, add the
export
line to your shell's configuration file (e.g.,
~/.zshrc
).
Tip:
You can also place your API key into a
.env
file at the root of your project:
OPENAI_API_KEY
=
your-api-key-here
The CLI will automatically load variables from
.env
(via
dotenv/config
).
Run interactively:
codex
Or, run with a prompt as input (and optionally in
Full Auto
mode):
codex
"
explain this codebase to me
"
codex --approval-mode full-auto
"
create the fanciest todo-list app
"
That’s it – Codex will scaffold a file, run it inside a sandbox, install any
missing dependencies, and show you the live result. Approve the changes and
they’ll be committed to your working directory.
Why Codex?
Codex CLI is built for developers who already
live in the terminal
and want
ChatGPT‑level reasoning
plus
the power to actually run code, manipulate
files, and iterate – all under version control. In short, it’s
chat‑driven
development
that understands and executes your repo.
Zero setup
— bring your OpenAI API key and it just works!
Full auto-approval, while safe + secure
by running network-disabled and directory-sandboxed
Multimodal
— pass in screenshots or diagrams to implement features ✨
And it's
fully open-source
so you can see and contribute to how it develops!
Security Model & Permissions
Codex lets you decide
how much autonomy
the agent receives and auto-approval policy via the
--approval-mode
flag (or the interactive onboarding prompt):
Mode
What the agent may do without asking
Still requires approval
Suggest
(default)
• Read any file in the repo
•
All
file writes/patches
•
All
shell/Bash commands
Auto Edit
• Read
and
apply‑patch writes to files
•
All
shell/Bash commands
Full Auto
• Read/write files
• Execute shell commands
–
In
Full Auto
every command is run
network‑disabled
and confined to the
current working directory (plus temporary files) for defense‑in‑depth. Codex
will also show a warning/confirmation if you start in
auto‑edit
or
full‑auto
while the directory is
not
tracked by Git, so you always have a
safety net.
Coming soon: you’ll be able to whitelist specific commands to auto‑execute with
the network enabled, once we’re confident in additional safeguards.
Platform sandboxing details
The hardening mechanism Codex uses depends on your OS:
macOS 12+
– commands are wrapped with
Apple Seatbelt
(
sandbox-exec
).
Everything is placed in a read‑only jail except for a small set of
writable roots (
$PWD
,
$TMPDIR
,
~/.codex
, etc.).
Outbound network is
fully blocked
by default – even if a child process
tries to
curl
somewhere it will fail.
Linux
– there is no sandboxing by default.
We recommend using Docker for sandboxing, where Codex launches itself inside a
minimal
container image
and mounts your repo
read/write
at the same path. A
custom
iptables
/
ipset
firewall script denies all egress except the
OpenAI API. This gives you deterministic, reproducible runs without needing
root on the host. You can use the
run_in_container

data.title: DPRK IT Workers in Open Source and Freelance Platforms
data.author: jtraglia
data.article_summary: 本文揭露了朝鲜IT工作者利用开放源代码和自由职业平台进行可疑活动的情况。作者发现一名可疑的提交者（0xExp-po）在一个合法的开发者项目中活动，经过两个月的调查，发现了更多朝鲜 actors，他们通过“PR垃圾邮件”和虚假身份在Web3平台上获取报酬。文章警告，这些平台缺乏严格的用户审核（KYC），可能助长朝鲜IT工作者的可信度及未来渗透能力，威胁开发者和用户安全。调查显示，这些 actors 使用伪造身份、操纵提交历史、窃取代码库，并通过自动化工具管理多个虚假身份。特别是平台“onlyDust”上，部分朝鲜IT工作者已获得报酬，呼吁各方加强安全审查。

43721754.article_content:
DPRK IT Workers in Open Source and Freelance Platforms
By:
blackbigswan
,
0xfigo
2025-04-16
DPRK
Investigation
DPRK IT Workers Leveraging Open Source and Freelance Platforms
On February 9, 2025, we discovered a suspicious actor within the repository of a legitimate developer. Initially, we informed the developer about the potential malicious intent of one of his active committers. This led us into a two-month-long process of discovering additional North Korean actors, “PR Spammers” and experiencing the subpar vetting process present in one of the “Pay for PR” (freelance) platforms in Web3.
First of all, this article is a call to action for any protocol or platform employing remote workers and open source contributors, especially when payments are made in cryptocurrencies and where low to no KYC is performed. Secondly, it’s a warning: avoidance of the issue by the affected platform may have consequences beyond it. By harboring DPRK IT Workers, you are allowing their credibility to grow, their future infiltration to be more effective, and you are putting developers and users outside of your platform at risk too.
Let’s start the tour of this extremely interesting activity, with twists, turns, and at least one ridiculous video call.
First Actor Discovered
The first identity we discovered belongs to a developer going by the handle
0xExp-po
on GitHub. The actor’s patterns of activity fit the known DPRK IT Workers’ M.O. We collected the evidence and informed the affected repository owner, a developer working on one of Stellar’s “Build on Stellar” programs. The developer acknowledged the issue and passed the information “up the chain”. At this point in the investigation, we did not yet realize how deeply connected the whole case was to the popular Web3 freelance platform
onlyDust
.
List of highly unusual patterns discovered:
Account created at
2023-12-10T13:54:11Z
; however, commit history manipulation displays account history dating back to 2018.
The actor opened the usual “Spam Issues” in several organizations already associated with “Account/Activity Farming” activities.
“Credibility building” through opening “Spam Issues” in valid organizations in exchange for badges displayed in the GitHub UI view.
Multiple repositories with “stolen” commit history (DPRK IT Workers
git clone
the original repository and edit its commit history before pushing it to their own profiles).
Toxic following/follower patterns (checked against our internal DB).
A strong connection to another suspicious actor we discovered later on.
Github Profile view
List of contributors to Tansu project on onlyDust.com
Amounts paid for work to the DPRK IT Worker (0xExp-po)
Second Actor and the Cluster Unwinds
0xExp-po
led us to
bestselection18
. A similarly, if not more, suspicious actor who was active in the repository of the same developer. We were already aware of
bestselection18
activity for some time before this investigation began, he was on a high-confidence list of suspicious actors from our past work. data.title: The "De" in "Decentralization" Stands for "Democracy"
data.author: NotInOurNames
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了Fediverse（联邦宇宙）的核心优势：网络本身比单个网站（实例）更重要。即使某个实例下线或消失，用户可以轻松迁移到其他实例，而无需让朋友一起转移，因为朋友们仍在同一个网络中。这种设计使得网络具有韧性，不像传统网站下线会造成用户流失。文章还提到，过去网站经常下线是常态，而Fediverse的这种特性让用户对实例下线习以为常。同时，Fediverse还提供了跨国迁移实例的灵活性，避免因政府或制裁等问题影响使用。总之，实例可消亡，但网络永存。

43720316.article_content:
I’m reminded of
something I read on the Fediverse yesterday
; I’ll quote it at length with no changes in formatting:
the secret sauce of the fediverse is that the network is the important part. the websites die but the network keeps going. even if your instance dies in a blaze of glory or whatever, you go somewhere else and your friends are still there.
you see nerds on other websites not understand this. they’re like “fedi instances go down all the time”. yeah, but individual instances don’t matter. your friends are still there. you just go to a different instance. you didn’t have to convince your friends to follow you on a different website because they keep going to the same one.
also, you gotta remember, websites went down all the time before now. that was just a fact of life before the modern age of the googles and the facebooks and such with giant data centers and 24/7 on call engineers. like it used to be websites would go down for a while and you’d say “well, i guess i’ll go somewhere else until Greg wakes up and fixes it”
we’re used to it by now. usually you get some warning when an instance is gonna go down permanently so you get a chance to ask your friends if they have room on their instance. it’s annoying, but, again, it’s less traumatic than having to leave, say, twitter, because you don’t have to convince your friends to move
instances die, the network lives on. as it should be.
meanwhile, if bluesky gets bought by hitler 2, you’re shit out of luck
you ever think about how eugen could quit this and pull the plug on mastodon.social tomorrow and we’d be basically fine
… also, like, if your instance gets a nastygram from a government, or if you can’t pay for your domain because of sanctions against the taliban, you can move to an instance in a different country. that’s pretty nice.

data.title: 4chan Sharty Hack And Janitor Email Leak
data.author: LookAtThatBacon
data.article_summary: In April 2025, the online community Soyjak.Party claimed to have hacked 4chan, restoring the deleted /QA/ board and leaking emails of 4chan "janitors" (moderators). The hackers exploited vulnerabilities in 4chan's outdated PHP code and deprecated MySQL functions, particularly in the yotsuba.php script that handles posts and moderation. Leaked information included a list of emails, some of which were .edu addresses. Although there were claims that some janitors used .gov emails, this remained unverified. The hack led to widespread discussion on platforms like Twitter (X), KiwiFarms, and Reddit. The incident was confirmed and widely reported across various internet forums and social media.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：4chan相关的技术漏洞、文化影响、及其变迁

不同观点：
• robotnikman指出，4chan的漏洞源于允许上传未验证的PDF文件，并通过过时的Ghostscript版本生成缩略图，导致攻击者可以通过PostScript命令获取系统访问权限。这一技术细节解释了此次黑客攻击的手法。

• shipscode认为，现代社交媒体（如Instagram、TikTok）相比4chan更加混乱和有害，尤其是doxxing和网络猎巫现象。他怀念早期4chan的“不是你的私人军队”心态，并认为那时的网络环境相对有底线。

• Red_Tarsius指出，很多人将4chan的/pol/板视为整个网站的代表，而实际上其他板如/tg/、/ck/、/fit/等有更积极、多样化的讨论。他强调了匿名性带来的专注讨论体验。

• CamelCaseName感叹“旧互联网”的消失，并提到此次泄露事件中，管理员的家庭地址和工作联系方式被公开，显示事件的严重性。

• cherryteastain提到4chan对科学的贡献，特别是对超级排列问题的研究，并希望人们记住这一点，而非仅关注其负面影响。

• TheAceOfHearts分享了KnowYourMeme上的额外细节，特别是关于词汇转换器（如SMH变为BAKA），增加了对事件背景的理解。

• EcommerceFlow认为/lit/板是一个发现好书的地方，其他平台因算法或投票机制无法提供真实的意见交流。

• helle253认为4chan的文化影响深远，但随着/pol/和/r9k/等板的影响扩大，4chan已不再如从前。他怀念早期/v/板的讨论氛围。

• cbg0批评4chan在2025年仍使用简单的HTTP认证来托管phpMyAdmin，认为这是明显的安全漏洞。

• praptak回忆早期4chan的技术缺陷，如直接将用户输入嵌入HTML，导致被griefers利用，显示了4chan早期安全措施的不足。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是4chan的文化变迁及其对互联网的影响。有些人认为4chan的早期文化相对有底线，而现代社交媒体更加混乱和有害；另一些人则关注4chan在技术上的安全漏洞及其带来的后果。
• 4chan的匿名性和特定板块的讨论质量被一些用户怀念和赞赏，而其极端内容和文化影响则被其他人批评。

About
April 2025 4chan Sharty Hack And Janitor Email Leak
refers to the
Soyjak.party
community's claimed hacking of 4chan in mid April 2025, which included the restoration of the deleted /QA/ board and leaking the emails of
4chan
"janitors," who are members of the site's moderation team. The attackers reportedly exploited outdated PHP code and deprecated MySQL functions in 4chan's backend, particularly in a core script named yotsuba.php, which manages post submissions and moderation. A Soyjak.Party users also shared a list of emails they claimed are associated with janitor and moderator accounts, including three .edu emails. Although some
internet
users claimed that the leaks included .gov emails associated with members of the moderation team, this remains unverified.
Origin
4chan was reportedly hacked by internet users claiming to be part of the Soyjak.Party community on April 14th, 2025. The hackers brought back the deleted /QA/ board, and temporarily granted access to 4chan's administrative site. An anonymous user posted about the hack on Soyjak.Party
[1]
around 10:05 PM EST. The thread contained several bits of leaked information, a look into the /j/ board as well as the entirety of the "yotsuba.php" code, which handles features like posting and reporting. Another post in the thread claimed to be leaking the email addresses associated with various janitors, three of which were .edu emails.
Early on April 15th, 2025, KiwiFarms
[3]
user Coberald posted a copy of the leaked 4chan source code. A user named Tofflenheim
[4]
also shared a link to an archive
[5]
of posts on /j/, a private board dedicated to janitor discussions.
Spread
X
[6]
user @Priniz_twt was one of the first to post about the hack on April 14th, 2025, gathering over 5,000 likes in less than a day.
On April 14th and April 15th, 2025, X
[2]
user @_yushe posted screenshots from the 4chan administrative page as well as analyzed the leaked "yotsuba.php" code, which handles features like posting and reporting. The post gathered over 500 likes in less than a day.
On April 15th, X
[7]
user @_yushe noted that 4chan was likely hacked because it was using an outdated version of PHP (a coding language used to run the site), which is full of known vulnerabilities, and deprecated (no longer supported) functions to handle its database.
Also on April 14th, X
[8]
user @LumpyTheCook tweeted, "Apparently 4chan is down because someone hacked the lead admin (Hiro) account and started leaking all the mod and janitor emails, contact info, chat logs, etc. Good job Hiro 👍" The thread also included the unconfirmed claim that some janitors were using .gov emails, (although some leaked lists did contained .edu emails).
On April 15th, 2025,
Redditor
/u/Meteorstar101 posted to the /r/greentext subreddit,
[9]
writing, "Last posts before 4chan got hacked," and showing the
Chicken Jockey
meme.

• ocschwar：批评特朗普政府无视布什报告中的理念，暗示其不重视科学进步。

主要讨论点：AI代码审查工具的创新、实用性、安全性及与其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• 支持与兴奋：[C-Pec]和[alexchantavy]对AI代码审查工具的创新表示兴奋，认为其能够提升代码审查体验，尤其是对于开源项目，能够帮助维持质量标准而不至于过于苛刻。[timfsu]也表示对该工具的支持，并提到它促进了团队的代码审查流程。
• 功能建议与期望：[justanotheratom]提出希望工具能够从开发者对话中自动生成自定义规则，并建议允许多种AI模型同时审查代码，通过反馈优化模型。[thuanao]则希望工具能够在本地运行，而不是在PR打开后才提供反馈。
• 实用性与适应性：[eqvinox]对工具的准确性表示担忧，认为如果工具不了解项目的自定义规则，其实用性会大打折扣。[dyeje]强调工具必须能够无缝集成到现有工作流中，而不是颠覆团队的现有流程。[kerryritter]对工具在Bitbucket上的不可用表示遗憾。
• 安全性与权限问题：[mdaniel]关注工具在数据安全和供应链攻击方面的潜在风险。[gslepak]则直接反对使用此类工具，认为其需要过高的权限，可能带来安全隐患。
• 与现有工具的比较：[pyfon]提到目前已有许多规则 based 工具，对AI工具的市场竞争表示怀疑。[bryanlarsen]对Graphite.dev的产品发展方向感到不满，因为其核心非AI产品似乎停滞不前。[bilalq]表示目前使用Graphite且满意，但对迁移到新工具持观望态度，关注定价和试用期。
• 针对特定场景的疑问：[ukuina]关心工具在大型单体仓库（monorepo）上的表现，尤其是对仓库大小和克隆操作的影响。

补充讨论：
• 工具的准确性与误报问题：[eqvinox]和[alexchantavy]提到工具在不同项目中的表现差异，以及误报和漏报的问题。
• 市场竞争与工具推广：[pyfon]和[bilalq]提到市场上的其他竞争工具，并关注工具的市场推广策略和定价模式。
• 工作流集成与用户体验：[dyeje]和[thuanao]强调工具集成和工作流适应性的重要性，关注工具对团队流程的影响和用户反馈的及时性。

争议焦点：
• 工具的权限与安全性：部分用户如[gslepak]对工具的高权限要求表示担忧，认为这可能带来安全风险，而其他用户如[alexchantavy]则更关注工具的功能和效率提升。
• 工具的实用性与误报问题：一些用户如[eqvinox]对工具在不了解自定义规则情况下的实用性表示怀疑，而其他用户如[timfsu]则对工具的实际效果表示满意。

总结：用户对AI代码审查工具的创新表示支持和期待，但也对其准确性、安全性、工作流集成和市场竞争等方面提出了具体关注和建议。

data.title: Wikipedia offers AI developers its article data on Kaggle to stop scraping
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 维基媒体基金会推出了一项人工智能就绪的数据集，在Kaggle平台上提供，旨在阻止AI公司从网站上自动抓取内容。该数据集包含高质量的JSON格式维基百科内容，如摘要、描述、信息框数据、图片链接和文章段落，不包括参考资料和非文字元素。通过提供预处理的数据，维基媒体希望减少对其服务器的负担，并方便开发者用于训练语言模型。该数据集已在4月15日发布，初期提供英语和法语版本，未来还将根据社区反馈进行改进。Kaggle是一个广泛使用的数据科学平台，拥有大量开放数据集。

UPDATED 12:05 EDT

APRIL 17 2025
AI
Wikipedia offers AI developers its article data on Kaggle to stop automated scraping
by
Kyt Dotson
SHARE
The Wikimedia Foundation, the organization behind the internet’s largest free encyclopedia
Wikipedia
, is offering an
artificial intelligence-ready dataset on Kaggle
that’s aimed at dissuading AI companies and large language model trainers from scraping the website.
“Instead of scraping or parsing raw article text, Kaggle users can work directly with well-structured JSON representations of Wikipedia content — making this ideal for training models, building features, and testing NLP pipelines,” Wikimedia said in the announcement on Wednesday.
Kaggle
is a data science and machine learning community owned and governed by Google LLC that hosts datasets and data science challenges.
The dataset upload is available as of April 15 and includes high-quality elements such as abstracts, short descriptions, infobox key-value data, image links and segmented article sections. It excludes references and non-prose elements such as images and charts themselves.
Because the content
is taken
from Wikipedia, it’s licensed under the
Creative Commons
, a widely open free use license that allows for sharing, adapting and remixing content.
It
is also licensed
under the GNU Free Documentation License, or GDFL, although
in some
cases
public domain or alternative licenses may apply.
“Kaggle is already a top place people go to find datasets, and there are few open datasets that have more impact than those hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation,” said Brenda Flynn, partnerships lead at Kaggle.
LLM developers depend heavily on data from the internet to train their models, but they get their datasets by scraping that data from public-facing websites. Web scraping is an automated process of extracting content, usually text and images, from websites using software that can be aggressive and adds additional load to web servers above and beyond
normal
human traffic.
That additional load is a costly performance hit for the web servers that
have to
bear it.
The scraped data
also must
be reformatted so that machine learning and AI workflows can
use it
for training data.
Wikimedia and Kaggle said in the joint announcement that this dataset
is designed
to short-circuit this scraping not just to reduce the need for this scraping behavior and lower the burden on Wikimedia’s web servers but also to provide already clean, pre-parsed and developer-friendly data.
Kaggle is host to more than 461,000 freely accessible datasets for AI and machine learning covering a wide variety of topics. Wikipedia’s dataset will join datasets on health (such as diabetes and cancer), finance (such as credit card fraud and the stock market) and social sciences (such as social media trends and education). There’s
even
a dataset containing nutrition information on
80 cereal products
and one about
UFO sightings
.
The new Wikipedia dataset is
available in French and English
language editions on Kaggle
as an early beta release
.
Since this is an early release, Kaggle is welcoming
feedback and discussions
about the dataset from the community
directly
.

data.title: Everyone knows your location, Part 2: try it yourself and share the results
data.author: mtlynch
data.article_summary: 作者在本文中分享了关于第三方位置数据共享的最新进展和更高效的分析方法。自首次发布相关内容以来，作者与多个领域的专家进行了讨论，并受邀参加播客探讨地理位置数据和隐私问题。为了简化和加速分析过程，作者开发了一个小型指南和一个Python笔记，允许任何人记录移动应用的流量并发现其中的有趣信息。初始设置需10-30分钟，每个应用的分析大约需要10分钟。作者还创建了一个Google表格和表单，供用户填写和查看他人评论，以众包方式收集应用数据共享的信息。此外，作者提供了可视化工具，帮助用户更直观地理解广告公司域名的分布及其请求频率。最终发现，Unity在移动游戏应用流量中占据主导地位。

43716704.article_content:
It's been more than 2 months now since my first post on the topic of location data sharing between various 3rd parties came out – in case you haven't seen it, you should definitely start from there:
Everyone knows your location
How I tracked myself down using leaked location data in the in-app ads, and what I found along the way.
tim.sh
tim
Since then I had a chat with a lot of people working in this field – both members of non-profit organisations, fighting for data privacy rights in various countries, and employees of adtech companies, proving my words right or wrong (but mostly right). I was even invited to "
Lock and Code
" podcast to talk about geolocation data and privacy. Ok, enough with the bragging.
I went through the process described in my initial post and decided to make it faster and more scalable: manually going through hundreds of requests in Charles was very cool for research and educational purposes, but it also took me a lot of time to find "interesting" requests coming from a single app.
I've significantly upgraded my approach (though it could definitely be more efficient), and in this post I wanted to share it with you.
TL;DR
I have created a small guide and a Python notebook that allow anyone to record mobile app traffic and find surprising things in it.
Here's
the link to a GitHub repo
with it.
The initial setup takes 10-30 minutes.
Analysis using this algorithm took me about 10 minutes per app - you can definitely dig deeper and get lost for hours if you find something interesting in there..
Follow the
readme
or the guide below if you'd like to try!
I came up with an idea
: it would take me hundreds of hours to go through each app and record the traffic, though I would love to do that – let's not blindly trust some table from the internet, but find out for ourselves.
I copied the Gravy Analytics Google Sheet and created a simple form that you can fill in (no personal info is collected) that writes to that Google Sheet
Link to the table
Look up any app you already have on your phone or just a random one in the table, check if others have commented on it already and record the traffic.
Finally, if you want to help crowdsource the information on the kinds of data the apps from the list collect and share –
fill in the form
:
I found something interesting in the app traffic
Hey! I don’t know how much people will go through with all the instructions and analysis, but since you’re here, you probably already did it and found something. Thanks for being here and doing this. Fill in the form below and your response will be recorded to a shared spreadsheet. PLEASE CHECK ALL OF YOUR INPUTS FOR YOUR PERSONAL INFORMATION. This form is set in a way that I collect nothing personal from you (like email or Google account or whatever), but your response will be viewable by virtually anyone - so be aware!
Google Docs
Please edit all the private information in your submission (in case it's there).
Visualising "domain power"
Before jumping into the guide, I wanted to share a few cool-looking visualisations with you.
Long story short: lately I've been obsessed with graph visualisations of things, especially branchy-embedded ones.
While analysing the traffic I found myself curious: how are the adtech companies domains distributed across all of the requests?
So I joined these two together and created a visualisation using
PyVis
that would answer that question:
Here's some context:
Every circle is a domain or a subdomain.
The hierarchy is represented by the inclusion of circles into others.
Example:
o-sdk.ads.unity3d.com
is represented by 3 circles:
o-sdk
inside of
ads
inside of
unity3d
.
Colors represent the app (I analysed 5) that the request corresponds to.
I used low opacities for better visibility, and it turns out that in my mix of colors and their opacities purple is the combination of all of them.
Circle sizes, or masses, represent the frequency: how often did this or that domain appear in the requests data.
See any insights?
Unity
rules the mobile game app traffic scene.
For comparison, the
g / doubleclick
thing is Google Ad Network.
Take a look at it in motion:
I included the code for it –
visualise_domains.ipynb
in the same repo so that you could create the same visualisation out of the data you record.
I also included the
ad_domains.html
file with this sample (mine) graph – simply open it in your browser if you want to play around with it.
I also was curious of the density of the requests – in my last post, I mentioned that hundreds of requests happen in just a few seconds, and now I could finally take a look at them:
Filenames in the legend are flows collected from 5 different games.
I cut it at 60s for better visibility, but obviously there were requests after that as well.
This one is again a different view of the domain power – look at the list on the right.
It should be obvious by now that Unity is the leader in this strange contest – it has the most subdomains called and the most requests mad

• [jane123]提到应用的加载速度有时较慢，询问是否有性能优化的计划，作者（timsh）回应称，性能问题已经在新的更新中得到解决，并感谢用户的反馈。

• [techenthusiast]进一步提出，希望看到一些数据安全和隐私保护方面的措施，作者（timsh）承诺会在后续的版本中加强这些方面的功能。

争议焦点：用户对应用功能和界面设计存在疑问，并希望作者能提供更详细的解释和改进方向，而作者则倾向于通过互动问答来回应这些疑问。

data.title: ChatGPT now performs well at GeoGuesser
data.author: dredmorbius
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GeoGuesser游戏中多模态LLM模型的表现及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• **对模型表现的肯定**：
  - [barcode_feeder] 认为模型表现惊人，尽管并非完美，但在识别多张无元数据图片的地理位置时表现良好，尤其是在一些著名地点（如韩国公园和美国城市）的识别上。
  
• **对模型表现的质疑**：
  - [actuallyalys] 认为仅凭几个例子不能证明GeoGuesser问题已被"解决"，并提出可能存在数据泄露的问题，且模型只是基于已有特征和猜测进行推断，而非真正解决所有场景。
  - [viraptor] 指出模型在识别热门地点上表现良好，但在处理乡村或不常见地点时仍存在困难，不能称之为完全"解决"。

• **对模型隐私影响的担忧**：
  - [iambateman] 认为随着LLM模型在图像识别上的进步，普通人也能轻易获取图片的地理信息，这对长期隐私保护构成威胁。
  
• **对模型识别机制的探讨**：
  - [Retr0id] 怀疑模型可能通过用户请求的IP等信息间接获取地理位置，而非完全依赖图像内容。
  - [romanhn] 对未来所有照片都能自动语义和地理标记表示期待，但同时也担忧隐私问题。

• **对隐私风险的实际测试**：
  - [Gathering6678] 通过实验发现，只要照片中没有明显地标且元数据被清除，ChatGPT在识别地理位置时会出错，认为隐私风险可控。

• **对模型应用场景的扩展讨论**：
  - [bhl] 认为在高密度城市环境中（如首尔的面包店或日本的寿司店）准确标记独特地点比GeoGuesser更难。
  - [jampa] 引用"Geoguesser Meta Iceberg"图，暗示新一代AI在GeoGuesser中的表现只是冰山一角。

• **对模型竞争力的评价**：
  - [usaar333] 引用Geobench.org的排行榜，指出该模型在GeoGuesser领域并非顶尖，质疑其实际竞争力。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户（如[xeonmc]和[ggnore7452]）对LLM模型的表现持中立或乐观态度，认为其在特定应用场景中表现良好，但并非完全解决所有问题。
• 技术细节上，[abcanddbutnote] 提到通过简单代码可以解决部分技术问题，暗示技术实现的复杂性因场景而异。

争议焦点：模型是否真正解决了GeoGuesser问题及其对隐私的潜在影响。

data.title: What do I think about Lua after shipping a project with 60k lines of code?
data.author: JSLegendDev
data.article_summary: 本文是Oleg Chumakov对Lua语言在项目开发中的使用体验，特别是通过与《Craftomation 101》主程序员Ivan Trusov的对话，总结了使用Lua编写的6万行代码项目的经验。选择Lua是因为Defold引擎原生支持Lua和C++，且Lua具有轻量化和易于嵌入的特点，适合跨平台和教育用途。Ivan提到，Lua缺乏一些常见编程特性如自增操作和"continue"语句，且数组索引从1开始，初期可能不习惯。但他认为Lua受功能性语言启发，可以应用一些功能性编程模式。Ivan还表示，Lua没有类机制，但通过简单的“表”结构实现代码组织，对他而言更加直观。总体而言，Lua在项目中表现良好，尽管有一些小缺点，但其灵活性和简洁性非常适合游戏开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lua语言的优缺点以及在实际项目中的应用和维护问题

不同观点：
• mabster认为，动态类型语言（如Lua）在维护大型代码库时可能会引发问题，特别是函数参数的灵活性会导致难以追踪的错误。他还提到Lua中表（tables）既可以作为字典也可以作为列表使用，这导致了某些bug。他更偏好静态类型语言或像Python和TypeScript这样可以添加类型的语言，以提高代码的可维护性。
• ksymph对Lua和Defold游戏引擎持积极态度，认为尽管Defold有学习曲线和一些 quirks，但它通过一些设计上的权衡引导开发者写出结构良好的代码。他推荐其他人尝试Defold。
• tc4v批评mabster的观点，认为其缺乏经验，并指出许多问题并不是Lua独有的，而是由于对类型注解和语言特性不熟悉导致的。
• nine_k指出，Lua在大型项目中是可行的，但对LuaJIT等工具未被提及感到惊讶。他还希望看到对使用Löve等其他引擎的大型游戏的分析。
• rahil627偏好love2D和dragonruby框架，但承认Defold在2D游戏开发中的优势，如提供游戏编辑器和模块化的游戏结构。
• jokoon使用Godot引擎和GDScript，认为如果引擎本身承担了大部分重任，脚本语言的速度并不是问题。
• xlii从Lua转向Fennel，认为Fennel更容易维护，并认为它足以替代Lua。

补充讨论：
• helsinki和suzzer99对代码格式和缩进发表了幽默评论，没有深入技术讨论。
• gnabgib和kragen引用了其他相关讨论和幽默解释，未深入技术细节。
• ludicrousdispla对文章中提到的“函数式风格”感到困惑，认为只是标准代码。
• nirav72和rendall提到了Lua在实际项目中的应用实例，如Beyond All Reason游戏和Roblox平台。kgeist补充提到Roblox拥有大量每日活跃用户，并使用Lua的变种语言。

争议焦点：
• mabster对Lua的可维护性提出质疑，而tc4v则认为这些问题源于开发者经验不足，而非Lua语言本身的缺陷。

43723088.article_content:
What do I think about Lua after shipping a project with 60,000 lines of code?
Oleg Chumakov
·
Follow
Published in
Luden.io
·
15 min read
·
May 30, 2024
--
1
Listen
Share
Hi there! This is Oleg from
Luden.io
. We decided to have a deep and meaningful conversation about Lua programming language with Ivan Trusov, lead programmer of the video game
Craftomation 101
. It contains ~60,000 lines of
Lua
code and is made with
Defold
game engine.
I asked Ivan to talk about the real issues and show real code, not the “hypothetical code, carefully prepared for the public to illustrate not how we do it but how we think it's supposed to be done.”
Craftomation 101
is a game about self-replicating robots, instructed with visual programming to craft (and eat) resources to terraform a frozen planet. The game was recently released to Early Access for Windows, macOS, and Linux on
Steam
,
itch.io
, and
GOG
. Also, there is
a free demo playable in the web browser
.
The game was well received by players and currently holds “Very Positive” user rating on Steam. Additionally, 2 months after the launch, a few educational organizations are using it for computer science classes and coding camps (which is so exciting and inspiring for us!)
Oleg Chumakov: Ivan, first of all, why Lua? Why have we not considered using TypeScript, Haxe, plain C++, or something else at the beginning of development?
Defold engine provides C++ and Lua support but there is an open-source TypeScript + Defold toolkit
https://ts-defold.dev/
and Haxe support library for Defold
https://github.com/hxdefold/hxdefold
The Defold engine was chosen for the project because it provides super lightweight web builds that are Chromebook-compatible and native builds for PCs, consoles, and mobile platforms. It’s important because our games are used in educational organizations full of Chromebooks.
Ivan Trusov:
I asked Dmitry…
Dmitry — a colleague of ours, and a veteran of Defold engine — told me that everything is cool with Lua. I asked him if Lua is the language we use to write config files for Redis. He assured me that everything is going to be great because he had already shipped a bunch of projects with it.
So I trusted Dmitry…
Ivan Trusov - lead programmer of Craftomation 101
My previous experience was with C++ (I thought I knew C++, but working with ClickHouse showed me otherwise), Python (though I was aware that Python wasn’t a big player in game development), and Java. So my stack was outside of major game development engines. Additionally, Defold provided native support for Lua and C++, making it an easy decision.
I heard that Lua is also known among game developers as an easily integrable, tiny language for any homebrew engine, especially when you want to provide more flexibility for your game designers in implementing complex in-game systems like abilities or spell effects.
On the flip side, you might occasionally find performance spikes in the profiler when game designers use some “dark magic” inside their Lua scripts.
But this integration as an additional language for game designers wasn’t our case; we intended to code all the game logic in Lua.
O.C.: So you started developing in Lua. Do you remember if anything surprised you about Lua in the beginning?
I.T.:
Sure, the lack of an increment operation, no “continue” instruction, and array indices starting from 1 instead of 0. These differences can be jarring, especially when switching between two languages for different projects/scripts. I still sometimes write
[array.length-1]
to get the index of the last element; you just can’t get used to that after years of working with C++ and Python.
Also, back in my university years, I took two courses on Haskell. Surprisingly, I see some benefits in applying approaches from functional languages to Lua. For example, creating an uncurried function with 4 steps, then folding and decorating it.
What I’m trying to say is that Lua was probably inspired by some functional elements along with simple scripting languages. This is why some functional patterns can bring new ideas to a Lua developer’s life.
Those functional vibes were quite surprising to me. I can illustrate it with something like this:
With syntactic sugar aka “Haskell vibes”
Without syntactic sugar aka “Haskell vibes”
Here is also a bit more complex illustration of “Haskell vibes” in Lua with
currying a function
and
an alternative solution
for comparison.
O.C.: And what about the lack of classes in Lua?
I.T.:
Actually, I always loved simple solutions and was never a fan of OOP. To create a good class, one needs to understand a lot about its future usage and OOP principles in general. I still cringe at memories of past programming job interviews that included questions like, “Tell me about the three principles of OOP”. Maybe some companies still ask about that during interviews. We don’t judge here.
The organization of code in Lua was quite intuitive to me. It was even clearer because of its' simple “everything is a table

data.title: CN Tower, Behind the Scenes (2014)
data.author: ianpenney
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是Roadwolf于2014年2月1日发布的，分享了他在CN Tower（加拿大国家电视塔）担任无线电台工程师期间拍摄的一些幕后照片。文章介绍了CN Tower的安保办公室、柴油发电机房、地下送货区以及通往SkyDome（天穹体育馆）的共用地下车库。还描述了用于将多个VHF和UHF商业频段无线电合并到CN Tower外部天线系统的Sinclair腔体调谐器，以及VE3TWR业余无线电中继器的位置。文章提到了旧的CKFM发射机（包括Continental和Collins的电子管发射机）以及新的Nautel固态发射机，并详细说明了Marconi合并器系统，该系统将九个FM电台合并到一个天线系统中，总输出功率达到约350,000瓦。最后，文章提到了CHUM FM和CHFI的设备，并简要介绍了CN Tower的电梯和楼梯历史。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕特殊地点和技术设备的讨论，包括CN塔的射频环境及其影响，以及对技术设备和其背后故事的兴趣。

不同观点：
• [分享体验] theyknowitsxmas 分享了一个关于电梯LED隐藏图片的视频链接，展示了电梯技术中隐藏的趣味性。
• [技术安装] ianpenney 提到社区成员在CN塔附近安装了Meshtastic节点，并分享了该地点的一些历史背景。
• [射频干扰] xattt 描述了在CN塔的太空甲板层使用模拟摄像机时遇到的射频干扰问题，指出该地点射频强度极高，导致设备出现视觉静电干扰。
• [未察觉技术设施] thisisnotauser 表示自己曾到访CN塔，但未注意到周围的射频发射设施，说明这些设施隔离良好。
• [类似体验] whalesalad 分享了自己在胡佛大坝涡轮机内部的经历，表达了对大型技术设备及其背后故事的兴趣，同时提到因设备被盗和缺乏备份而丢失珍贵照片的遗憾。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：xattt 提到的射频干扰问题与 thisisnotauser 未察觉到射频发射设施形成对比，显示出对同一地点技术设施的不同体验和认知。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：不同用户对技术设备内部及其特殊环境的探索和分享，体现出对科技和工程的浓厚兴趣。

总结：评论主要围绕CN塔和其他大型技术设施的内部体验和技术细节展开，用户们分享了自己的亲身经历、技术设施的影响以及对设备背后故事的兴趣。

43723086.article_content:
Home
Categories
Urban Exploration
CN Tower
Posted by Roadwolf on February  1, 2014
Here are some of the photos from back in my radio station engineer days.  The following are some photos of the CN Tower, behind the scenes.
CN Tower Security Office
This is the CN Tower Security office.  The hallway straight ahead is the hallway to the underground delivery area.  On the left side along the hallway is the Diesel Generator Room.  This photo was taken from a position in front of the maintenance Elevator.
To the right just down the hall is the exit to the stairway which exits out to the patio in Bobbie Rosenfeld Park.  The underground delivery area is accessed through a shared underground garage with the 'SkyDome'.  It can be seen at the corner of Rees and Bremner Road.
This rack of Sinclair cavity tuners was used to combine many VHF and UHF commercial band radios into a single set of antennas on the outside of the CN Tower.  The antennas can be seen above the main pod, attached to the cement structure a hundred or so feet above the pod, facing towards the city.  The VE3TWR ham radio site utilizes this antenna system as well.  The access door behind the rack, is how you access the crawl space between this level (Level 5) and the curved metal roofing material which the edge walk circles around.
VE3TWR Ham Radio Repeater
In fact, the VE3TWR repeater is directly beside this rack, hidden between it and the access door.
CKFM's old Continental and Collin's tube transmitters.
CKFM's old tube transmitters.  One a Continental Electronics and the other a Collins.  I believe they were both about 26kw units, but we only ran them at about 20kw.
CKFM's new Nautel solid-state transmitter.
They were likely replaced by this.  A Nautel solid state modular FM Transmitter.
The old CKFM equipment rack.  You can see this behind the new transmitter in the photo up above.
The modular design of the new Nautel allowed hot swapping of the various power modules.  They all fed into a center combiner.
Kind of a crazy looking device, but very slick in my opinion.
It is a mini version of the large combiners up in the CN Tower, which combine all the radio stations up there into one of two antenna feeds.  The Marconi CN Tower Combiner.
This combined nine FM stations into a single antenna system.  I believe it had the capacity to handle 12 stations.  Each station put in about 10 kilowatts to 30 kilowatts depending on their license.  The total output of the antenna array had an ERP of about 350,000 watts supposedly.
One of the mechanical COAX switches on the MARCONI combiner system.
A view between a few of the FM Combiners.  The copper pipes are actually rigid coaxial 'cables'  The large pipes close to the ceiling in the background are about 10 inches wide, and feed the antenna arrays.  The equipment in the background is the processing system for the DAB Radio equipment.  The other pipes are actually silver clad rigid coaxial pipes.
A closer view of the combiner status board.
The transmitters in this room alone are drawing just a little bit of power.  :D  As I vaguely recall, there was a small gen set up there, to specifically service the FM Transmitters.
CHUM FM's Collins FM Transmitter and new Nautel Transmitters in background.
CHUM FM also had an old Collins and some new Nautels.
CHFI's CN Tower Equipment Rack
I believe this was CHFI's rack, with some nice PSB monitor speakers.  Really overkill for such a loud/high noise environment.  But nice none the less.
CHFI's Continental Transmitters
CHFI's
Continental Electronics
transmitters I believe.  Standardization is great.
'Outside' area of Level 5.
This was a view out the access door shown in one of the first photos above.  The wall on the right is the wall to the transmitter room, and the metal angled wall is the wall to the outside.  You ca kinda see some light between the metal slats and you can definitely feel air moving around up there.  It is effectively outside.  This is the part of the CN Tower that people walk around with with edge walk.
Various levels of the Main Pod. Image taken from Wikipedia and Edited by me.
So there ya go.  A little behind the scenes tour of places you likely don't see very often.

data.title: I analyzed chord progressions in 680k songs
data.author: jnord
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了作者分析了来自Ultimate-Guitar网站的68万首歌曲的和弦进程数据，发现了一些有趣的规律。作者首先解释了基本音乐概念，如音符、和弦等，然后展示了最常见的20个和弦，其中G大和弦和C大和弦最为普遍，占所有和弦的24%。不同音乐流派之间的和弦选择差异显著，例如，乡村音乐常用大调和弦，而爵士乐中7和弦更为常见。这种差异部分源于各流派常用乐器的不同，如爵士常用小号（调为Bb），而乡村音乐常用班卓琴（调为G）。通过将和弦分类并按年代分析，作者还发现不同年代和弦使用的趋势变化，例如7和弦和强力和弦在特定流派和年代中更流行。文章通过数据展示了音乐中丰富的和弦多样性及其随时间和流派的变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对和弦分析方法及其数据集的有效性和局限性的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持使用相对和弦分析（罗马数字分析）**：
  - huimang和memset认为绝对和弦分析不合理，应使用相对和弦分析以捕捉歌曲的结构和和弦关系。他们指出，忽略重复和弦会使分析失真，因为重复和弦是音乐形式的一部分（如布鲁斯）。
  - memset进一步建议将和弦转换为罗马数字以分析常见模式，以便更好地区分不同音乐类型（如乡村和爵士）。

• **对绝对和弦分析的批评**：
  - huimang和cjohnson318指出，仅列出“最常见和弦”并不特别有用，更有意义的是分析相对常用和弦或和弦过渡（如从F到C的概率）。
  - mastazi和vthommeret提到，爵士乐中常见和弦（如D和A）在锐调中的频率高于预期，且爵士和弦多为maj7或6和弦，而非仅三和弦。

• **数据集及其来源的局限性**：
  - memset、hirvi74和alexjplant批评了原始数据集的构建方法和Ultimate Guitar的转录质量，指出其可能存在的错误和简化。
  - hirvi74特别提到数据集可能包含重复歌曲和仅限于吉他谱的问题，且现代音乐的简化和乐器可得性影响了分析结果。
  - throwaway0665和1337shadow指出，用户贡献的Ultimate Guitar谱往往会简化实际和弦，并可能使用变调夹，进一步影响分析准确性。

补充讨论：
• **对音乐复杂性和历史性的讨论**：
  - hirvi74提到音乐历史和不同乐器的可得性影响了音乐的复杂性，并质疑过度解读数据集结果的合理性。
  
• **工具和资源推荐**：
  - vthommeret推荐了Hooktheory作为更适合的和弦分析工具，提供相对和绝对和弦分析功能。

• **其他技术细节讨论**：
  - divbzero和zzo38computer讨论了和弦频率和和弦进程分析的区别，强调应考虑调号和非和弦音等因素。
  - jancsika对“间隔”和“二元组”的定义进行了技术性纠正。

争议焦点：绝对和弦分析与相对和弦分析的有效性，以及数据集的准确性和代表性。

Welcome back to
Can’t Get Much Higher
, where music and data meet. Before we get into this week’s topic, here are some recent pieces that people have enjoyed:
“
The Greatest Two-Hit Wonders
”
“
The Audiophile's Streaming Service: A Conversation with Qobuz's Dan Mackta
”

Revisiting the Death of the Key Change
”

How Many Artists Did The Beatles Kill?
”

How a Funeral Home Became Warner Records

Now, onto a big dataset about chords.
I Analyzed the Chord Progressions of 680k Songs
By Chris Dalla Riva
Chordonomicon. I couldn’t get the word out of my head. Every syllable was just as beautiful as the last. Try saying it. Kord-oh-nom-i-con. It sounds like a mystical word. And, for me, it is. But it’s a term that didn’t exist last year.
“Chordonomicon” was coined by 5 researches last October when they needed a name for a new project that they’d just completed. This project pulled together
chord progressions and genres for nearly 680,000 songs
from the popular music learning website
Ultimate-Guitar
. I knew I had to do something with the data. But what?
A screenshot of
Ultimate-Guitar
, a popular music learning website
Typically, when I write a data-driven piece for this newsletter, my approach is somewhat scientific. First, I have a hypothesis, like “
there has been an increase in music biopics over the last few years
.” Then I find some data to test that hypothesis. Whether I’m correct or not, I publish the results. For example, when I looked at music biopics, I found that on an absolute basis there was a dramatic increase over the last few years, but on a relative basis, the peak was in the 1940s.
I didn’t really have a hypothesis to test with the Chordonomicon dataset, though. I just wanted to explore what was in there. There had to be something interesting among 680,000 chord progressions. And there was. But, first, we should start with a simple question: What’s a chord?
If you’re looking for in depth discussions on music theory, I’m not your guy. (You should probably turn to someone like
Ethan Hein
and his newsletter
Ethan teaches you music
.) But for this case, I think some basic definitions will help. A “note” is a single pitch. When you hit one key on the piano, for example, you are playing a note. An “interval” is a combination of two notes. A “chord” is a combination of three or more unique notes (e.g., a C major chord is comprised of the notes C, E, and G).
Above you can see a breakdown of the top 20 most common chords across the nearly 52 million chords notated in the Chordonomicon dataset. If you’ve ever played a guitar or piano, you won’t be surprised by the fact that G major and C major are at the top, accounting for 24% of all chords. These are some of the first chords you learn on those instruments. What’s interesting is that chord choices differ when you look across genre.
Below you can see a usage comparison of 20 common chords in jazz and country. The differences are stark. In country, for example, five major chords — G major, C major, D major, A major, and F major — comprise 61% of all chords played. Among jazz songs, by comparison, those chords only make up 39% of total chords. Nevertheless, if we take a look at some other chords, the relationship flips. Bb major, for example, makes up 2.6% of all chords in our jazz sample. For country, it’s 1.4%, almost half.
What explains these differences? Of course, some of it is connected to arbitrary compositional choices. But another piece is explained by the instruments used in each genre. For example, the trumpet is commonly used in jazz, and trumpets are tuned to Bb. Similarly, banjos and guitars are common in country. Banjos are tuned to open G, and, as noted, chords like G, C, and D are some of the first you will learn when picking up the guitar.
Looking at individual chords across a bunch of genres is a bit chaotic, though. Instead, we can group chords into a few categories to make cross-genre comparisons a bit more digestible. Below we can see that while your simple, three-note major chords (e.g., A major, Db major) are the most common across every genre, there are some stark differences in other categories. 7th chords, for example, are 2.5 to 13 times more common in jazz than any other genre. Similarly, power chords are 2 to 21.5 times more common in punk than any other genre. Furthermore, Suspended, diminished, and augmented chords basically don’t exist in rap.
But it’s not just interesting to compare these chord categories across genre. It’s interesting to compare them over time. Below you can see the prevalence of each chord type by decade from the 1930s to the 2020s. The most striking trend

data.title: Potatoes in the Mail
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: USPS允许直接邮寄土豆，无需盒子。只需在土豆上写上收件人和寄件人地址，称重后支付相应邮费即可寄出。这是USPS的一项有趣服务，被称为"SPUDTACULAR"。类似于椰子，土豆也可以作为独特的礼物寄送给别人。这项服务展示了邮政系统的灵活性和趣味性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过邮政系统邮寄各种 unusual 物品的可行性及趣闻

不同观点：
• [neilv] 认为可以通过邮寄像椰子这样的不寻常物品，并分享了个人经历，将椰子从夏威夷邮寄到波特兰，甚至成功种植出了一棵棕榈树。
• [paulkrush] 分享了关于邮票和邮寄技巧的见解，例如使用旧邮票以节省邮费，以及讨论了邮寄不寻常物品（如薄木片明信片）的可能性。他还提到使用小额率邮箱时重量限制的问题，建议避免让邮递员搬运过重的物品。
• [1024core] 讲述了在邮政中心目睹活鸭被邮寄的经历，表达了对邮寄活物的震惊。
• [ipcress_file] 分享了通过加拿大邮政的"monotainer"服务跨国搬运物品的经历，认为这是一种高效的搬家方式。
• [zkms] 提到了多家提供邮寄土豆服务的网站，并表示曾使用过其中一家服务，暗示这种新奇的邮寄方式正在流行。

补充讨论：
• [brk] 提到了Wired杂志的一篇文章《Return To Sender》，但未展开具体讨论。
• [thecosas] 提到了邮寄砖块的可能性，并提供了相关资料链接。
• [shoo] 分享了一篇关于纽约 pneumatic mail tubes 历史的详细文章，包括其工作原理、历史趣闻和系统维护等内容。
• [m463] 提到多年前有人尝试通过邮政系统邮寄各种物品，包括滑雪板和现金，但未能找到具体文章。
• [bredren] 对邮资的粘贴方式提出了疑问，担心如果使用邮票可能会脱落。
• [1024core] 再次提到邮政系统的多样性，并提供了一个链接。
• [Ninjinka] 提到了一本儿童百科全书，其中介绍了如何邮寄不寻常物品。
• [thallavajhula] 对在技术论坛上讨论邮政趣闻表示欣赏。
• [pmags] 对发现真实存在的邮寄土豆网站感到惊喜，并计划将其作为生日卡片送给 siblings。
• [memhole] 认为邮政系统可以邮寄各种奇怪物品，并提议组织公司活动来邮寄不寻常物品以增加趣味性。

争议焦点：
• 邮政系统邮寄活物（如鸭子）的合法性及伦理问题，[1024core] 对此表示震惊，而其他评论未深入探讨此问题。
• 使用旧邮票的有效性及经济性，[paulkrush] 认为这是一种省钱的方法，但未提及邮政局的官方立场。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 邮寄不寻常物品（如椰子、土豆、砖块）的实际操作及趣闻。
• 历史上 pneumatic mail tubes 系统的工作原理及趣闻。
• 现代邮政服务中"monotainer"等特殊服务的使用体验。

data.title: Memory Size Matters to PostgreSQL
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了PostgreSQL中用于管理共享缓冲区内存的机制，特别是时钟扫描（clock sweep）算法。共享缓冲区用于在数据库和后台之间传输数据页。早期版本使用简单的LRU算法，但因其局限性，PostgreSQL 8.0.0引入了自适应缓存替换（ARC），然而由于专利问题，后续版本替换为效率较低的2q算法，最终在8.1版本中采用了当前的时钟扫描算法。

时钟扫描通过"nextVictimBuffer"指针循环查找可替换的缓冲区。若缓冲区被固定或使用计数非零，则跳过。若缓冲区脏污，需先写入磁盘。当自由列表为空时，算法会遍历整个共享缓冲区以寻找替换候选。

这种机制在所有缓冲区都有效时会进行全缓冲区扫描，确保缓冲区管理的并发性和效率。在批量操作时，该策略可能会被覆盖，导致共享缓冲区的完全重写。
